brief: Rung 4a — a weather nobody has seen. RIVER MIST on still, clear mornings: a rate-capped scalar mistF() 0..1 in the cloudCover()/wetF() family that rises off the water around sunUp when the night was cold or wet (warmth < ~0.65, windF() < 0.3, cloudCover() low, wetF() > 0.3 OR warmth < 0.4 — price the rule with a probe so it opens on roughly a third of shoulder-season mornings and few midsummer ones) and burns off by ~sunUp + 3 h with the sun's height. Consumers, live not cached: a veil pass in drawScene() over the river columns and the low east ground (the far bank, the plaza's quay side) whose alpha falls with distance from the water — pale, desaturating, so the mill and the church tower stand out of it; HAZE (the backdrop's tint, already read by drawRoofRow at 0.55) mixes toward the mist colour; lamp halos in applyLight() widen while mistF() > 0; the sill names it ('mist on the river' in the ticker/nameAt when the pointer is over the water). The morning lapse (sunUp + 0.5) must land INSIDE it on a mist morning, so a visitor's second clock tap can show it.
successLooksLike: On a mist morning the wide shot at sunUp + 0.5 h shows the river and far bank softened to pale grey with the towers and the mill's lamp standing clear, the near lane sharp; by 09:30 it is gone with no frame the filmstrip's pops.mjs flags; probes/mist-year.mjs shows the fraction of mornings it opens by season and that it never opens in wind or rain.
avoid: Do not put the veil in the ground cache (it changes every frame) and do not step it — it is a rate-capped scalar with a cap, a cycle and an anchor (the law): mistF() = 0 must reproduce HEAD's pixels exactly. Do not add a mist to the night: the veil reads daylight, and nightF's multiply must stay last (the night-colour law). Do not open it after 09:00 or while it is raining.
